calibration.reason: Clear labels and a legible, familiar layout support the task, but misplaced focus after invalid input is a meaningful usability and craft flaw.

primary_action.input: Tab to the 6 m footbridge row, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show the path closed, ferry stopped and footbridge closed.
primary_action.observed: All three statuses updated, the count became 3 of 3, and the waterline reached the 6 m mark. Focus remained visible on the footbridge row.

A-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab twice and Enter set 2 m. The path was closed; ferry and footbridge remained listed as level not reached.
A-1440.fact_check: The rendered waterline aligns with 6 m and agrees with the displayed value and threshold labels. Real-world closure thresholds are not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The large cross-section connects each crossing to its elevation, with results visible alongside it.
A-1440.weakness: The threshold rows look like status rows, so their direct-jump behavior is not obvious.
A-1440.repair: Give the rows an explicit selection affordance or short instruction while retaining the visible focus outline.

primary_action.input: Tab to the 6 m footbridge row, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show all three affected crossings.
primary_action.observed: The value became 6 m, the waterline reached 6 m, and all three closure statuses appeared. The complete result was readable within the initial 390 by 844 viewport.

A-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab twice and Enter set 2 m; only the path was marked closed, while the other two rows said level not reached.
A-390.fact_check: The 6 m waterline matches the displayed level and diagram scale. Real-world thresholds are unsupported by the view.
A-390.strength: The diagram, control and complete status list fit together on the first mobile viewport.
A-390.weakness: The diagram labels are small, and the rows' ability to set a level is visually implicit.
A-390.repair: Increase diagram label legibility and indicate that threshold rows are selectable.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and list the path, ferry and footbridge closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m became selected, all three results appeared, and the waterline rose to the 6 m guide. Focus remained visible on 6 m.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m and left only the riverside path in the result list.
B-1440.fact_check: The 6 m waterline aligns with the 6 m guide and the result heading. Real-world closure thresholds are not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The clear level choices and concise results make the requested comparison quick.
B-1440.weakness: The illustrated ferry remains drawn below the 6 m waterline, which can read as submerged even though the text says it stops.
B-1440.repair: Place the ferry at the selected water surface or explicitly depict it as out of service.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three affected crossings.
primary_action.observed: 6 m became selected, the three results appeared, and the waterline aligned with 6 m. The complete result and diagram were readable within the initial 390 by 844 viewport.

B-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m and the result list contained only the riverside path closure.
B-390.fact_check: The selected value, result heading and 6 m waterline agree. Real-world thresholds are unsupported by the view.
B-390.strength: The choices and complete result precede the compact illustration, keeping the task easy to scan.
B-390.weakness: The small ferry appears below the selected water surface at 6 m, making the illustration less literal.
B-390.repair: Keep the ferry aligned with the water surface and distinguish its stopped state visually.

preference.reason: B makes the three level choices explicit, reaches 6 m with one arrow key from the default, and presents only the applicable closures. Its mobile result is complete and easy to scan in the first viewport. A's cross-section is strong, but its direct-jump rows are less discoverable.
